"On this page, you can monitor and view the status of your device.

CPU usage: here you can view real-time processor usage for each core, such as the current frequency or current usage percentage.

GPU usage: here you can view real-time graphics processor usage, such as the current frequency or current usage percentage.

Memory usage: here you can view the real-time RAM and ZRAM (virtual memory) usage. For RAM it shows the current frequency or current usage percentage, and for ZRAM (virtual memory) it shows the usage percentage and the compression algorithm being used.
 - Show memory: lets you choose whether to show the usage or the available RAM or ZRAM memory.

Thermal status: here you can view the temperature of the CPU, GPU, and battery in Celsius or Fahrenheit.
 - Use Fahrenheit unit: lets you choose whether to show the unit in Fahrenheit or Celsius for the temperatures.

Battery status: here you can view the battery's capacity or health."

"This page contains settings that provide basic optimization options.

System settings: this section offers options that are normally hidden from the user (It's recommended to leave default settings).
 - Optimize all apps: recompiles all apps with ART, both system and installed ones, using their real usage profile so they use less CPU when opening, improving performance and battery.
 - Battery optimizations on apps: restricts the background processes of apps.
 - Freeze cached apps: freezes background apps, improving battery by not using the CPU.

Kernel settings: this section offers options that work at kernel level, so they may or may not work properly depending on the kernel being used (It's recommended to leave default settings).
 - Wakelock blocker optimizations: prevents processes or events from keeping the phone awake for internal tasks (monitoring, network scanning, events, etc.), improving battery consumption at idle (may slightly delay notifications or network reconnections).

CPU settings: this section offers options such as efficiency or heat management (It's recommended to leave default settings).
 - CPU hotplug optimizations: improves efficiency when the CPU turns its cores off or on and improves performance stability, improving battery consumption when the device is idle.
 - Power efficient: improves the CPU power consumption by running tasks on the cores that are already active, avoiding waking the other idle cores, improving battery over time.
 - Thermal optimizations: reduces the CPU temperature by applying light thermal and AC current limits at kernel level, which reduces the heat generated by the device, but may slightly reduce system performance.
 - CPU efficiency boost: reduces high CPU usage spikes, which improves battery consumption over time.

GPU settings: this section offers options such as efficiency boost, etc. (It's recommended to leave default settings).
 - GPU efficiency boost: reduces high GPU usage spikes, slightly reduces the graphics load and applies a low-power profile, which improves battery over time.

Memory settings: this section offers options related to (ZRAM) virtual memory optimizations (It's recommended to leave default settings).
 - ZRAM optimizations: reduces how often the kernel moves apps from RAM to storage and vice versa, also reduces the ZRAM (virtual memory) compression intervals and keeps its cache for longer, reducing CPU usage, which improves battery consumption.

Storage settings: this section offers settings to improve UFS energy efficiency (It's recommended to leave default settings).
 - Storage optimizations: tunes the kernel to reduce the work done on each storage operation, with no I/O entropy and lighter I/O completion, thus reducing CPU usage, but it may slightly reduce read and write performance.

Battery settings: this section offers battery charging protection options, among others.
 - Battery charging protection: limits the maximum charging percentage to protect the battery and extend its health."

Make sure that battery protection on system is disabled to avoid conflicts/issues.
You can check this in Settings app > Battery > Battery protection.

You may need to re-plug the charger for the changes to take effect.

It\'s recommended to optimize applications every two weeks or after performing major system updates, this helps improve both performance and battery efficiency on device.\n\nNote: device may heat up during optimization and process may take several minutes.
DON\'T close the app during optimization!\nThis process may take several minutes...

WARNING: touching these options without knowing what you are doing can cause INSTABILITY or FREEZE on your device, depending on frequency and/or undervoltage settings you are using and some frequencies may not work depending on the kernel you are using.

"This page contains advanced options such as CPU core frequency options or undervoltage options for each component.

Frequency settings: this section contains frequency-related settings to allow you to control processing speed for little (efficiency) and big (performance) cores (It's recommended to leave default settings).
 - Max little cores frequency: limits the maximum frequency the little CPU cores (efficiency cores) can reach.
 - Max big cores frequency: limits the maximum frequency the big CPU cores (performance cores) can reach.

Undervolt settings: this section contains options related to voltage intensity for each device component, these are based on percentage margins, each slider bar offers undervoltage values, such as CPU, GPU, RAM, display, audio, etc. (It's recommended to leave default settings).
 - Little cores margin: lets you reduce the voltage percentage margin of the little CPU cores (efficiency cores).
 - Big cores margin: lets you reduce the voltage percentage margin of the big CPU cores (performance cores).
 - GPU margin: lets you reduce the voltage percentage margin of the GPU.
 - RAM margin: lets you reduce the voltage percentage margin of the RAM.
 - AUDIO margin: lets you reduce the voltage percentage margin of the device audio (speakers).
 - CAMERA margin: lets you reduce the voltage percentage margin of the camera modules (camera sensors).
 - CP margin: lets you reduce the voltage percentage margin of communications (mobile networks, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, etc.).
 - DISPLAY margin: lets you reduce the voltage percentage margin of the device display.
 - FSYS margin: lets you reduce the voltage percentage margin of the device storage, removable memory (SD card) and storage connected via USB.
 - INT margin: lets you reduce the voltage percentage margin of the device chipset buses.
 - INTCAMERA margin: lets you reduce the voltage percentage margin of the camera ISP (image signal processor).
 - IVA margin: lets you reduce the voltage percentage margin of the video codecs.
 - SCORE margin: lets you reduce the voltage percentage margin of the image and video vision coprocessor.

Note: increasing the frequency/speed will increase the heat generated by the device and these settings may make your device UNSTABLE or cause FREEZES depending on frequency and/or undervoltage settings you are using."

"This page displays information about app version, updates, experimental features, etc.

Import/Export: save or load app settings from a file.
 - Import settings: lets you load the app settings.
 - Export settings: lets you save the app settings.

Experimental: features that are still in testing but stable enough for the public (These options are disabled by default).
 - Background app process limit: limits the apps that can stay open in the background.
 - Force Doze on device idle: forces the device to enter deep sleep immediately after the device screen is locked.
 - Disable network service discovery: disables the automatic search for local network services to reduce background traffic, but apps will not be able to find devices such as Chromecast, printers or other nearby devices (slightly reduces battery consumption)."
